issues.body: RustScalar::String routes every accepted datatype through scalar_string, which only checks the datatype IRI and copies the lexical form. Consequently an xsd:integer field accepts values such as "not-an-integer", and the same issue affects xsd:decimal and other constrained datatypes lowered to String. SHACL's datatype constraint requires a well-formed lexical representation, and the README describes sh:datatype as a checked scalar, so the generated reader can accept data that violates the represented structural datatype constraint. The new beyond-i64 test proves range preservation but never tests an invalid xsd:integer lexical form.
issues.fix_hint: Preserve String as the output representation while adding datatype-specific lexical validation before copying it (at minimum for every recognized XSD datatype mapped to String). Add generated-loader cases proving a valid beyond-i64 xsd:integer loads and a malformed xsd:integer lexical form returns LoadError::LexicalForm.
issues.title: String-backed XSD datatypes accept malformed lexical forms

issues.body: xsd:long, xsd:int, xsd:short, and xsd:byte all use scalar_i64, which only parses as i64. This accepts out-of-range values for the narrower datatypes, such as "2147483648"^^xsd:int or "128"^^xsd:byte. The lowering comment says these mappings represent each datatype's complete value space without loss, but a checked reader must also reject values outside that datatype's value space.
issues.fix_hint: Make integer parsing aware of the actual datatype and enforce the XSD bounds for int, short, and byte after parsing (long already matches i64). Add generated-loader tests for each boundary and at least one just-outside value, asserting LoadError::LexicalForm or a more specific typed error.
issues.title: Narrow signed integer datatypes are not range-checked

verdict.summary: Round 2 fixes both prior major findings: unbounded xsd:integer is retained as String and exercised beyond i64::MAX, and Self is now reserved with a focused regression test. However, the generated reader still does not implement the advertised checked-scalar behavior completely. String-backed constrained datatypes accept malformed lexical forms, while the shared i64 parser accepts values outside the narrower xsd:int/short/byte value spaces. These are new major correctness findings, so progress is regressing under the required rubric despite the prior fixes.
